body.text:
**The review UI is live — try it right now:**

```
cd C:\src\git-for-ai
git for-ai review
```

Your browser opens to the local review app: the masthead shows HEAD, capture status, and index state; five stat cards (25 commits, 20 changes, 19 agent / 1 human, 17 sessions, 2 models); a "Needs attention" strip correctly flagging the five pre-capture milestone commits; and the filterable timeline — click any change to drill into its reasoning, and any session to read the trace as a narrative. Dark/light follows your system. It's `127.0.0.1`-only, read-only by construction (write methods get a 405), makes zero external requests, and serving the entire surface provably leaves every git ref byte-identical — I re-verified the build (4/4 packages), all 144 CLI+UI tests, and smoke-tested the live server myself before committing (`8543c62`).

The greyed-out Ask panel at the bottom says "Arrives with M12" — and that's exactly what I'm doing next: wiring `git for-ai ask` and `blame --why` over the committed query engine, plus the `/api/ask` endpoint so that panel lights up. With your key now set, the first question this repo answers about itself will come back as cited prose. That's the last step of this arc — from there the CLI lacks only `config`, `sync`, `doctor`, and `export` to be feature-complete against its reference.
M12 is the last piece of this arc — launching it now with full ownership of the CLI files (no other agents running):

M12 is underway. The agent is wiring both commands over the committed query engine — `git for-ai ask "<question>"` and `git for-ai blame --why <file>:<line>` rendering the exact output formats the architecture specified from day one — plus the `/api/ask` endpoint and the review UI's ask panel going from greyed-out to live.

Its definition of done is the payoff moment itself: a real dogfood run on this repo asking *"why was the server ref-relay tier eliminated?"* with the real embedding model and your real key (read from the user-level environment at spawn, never printed) — plus a `blame --why` on the R4 resolver code whose redesign we lived through two days ago. I've asked for the actual answers verbatim in its report, so you'll see exactly what the system says about its own history, citations and all.

When it lands I'll do the usual: independent build + test verification, personally re-run the dogfood, and commit. At that point the original CLI plan's "first genuinely satisfying moment" checklist — init, work captured, intent in the log, `blame --why` giving reasoning, `ask` giving a sourced answer — will be complete end to end, with only `config`, `sync`, `doctor`, and `export` left for the full reference, and the MCP server next on the approved roadmap after that.

Added as task #14, marked lower priority and explicitly held until the M12 agent releases the review-UI files. I captured your constraint precisely: this is a *re-prioritization*, not a reduction — ask panel promoted to the top once it's live, the timeline and change details rethought around what a human wants first (evidence and risk flags up front, progressive disclosure for the rest), but every piece of information stays present and reachable, both for thorough human review and for agents reading the page or its API.

One design thought worth noting in advance for when we get there: the cleanest way to honor "humans first, agents keep everything" may be to treat the JSON API as the agent surface (it already carries 100% of the data unconditionally) and let the visual layer be as opinionated as we like — that way the human page can get genuinely aggressive about hierarchy without ever constraining what an agent can read. We can debate that when the task comes up.

Meanwhile M12 is still running; the ask/blame dogfood report is the next thing you'll see from me.

That's a cleaner division than my hedge, and I've rewritten the task to match: **the review page is yours** — designed purely around what you want to see, with the ask box as the primary interaction at the top — while the CLI's `--json` output remains the complete, stable contract that agents read. The page owes agents nothing, which frees the redesign to be genuinely opinionated: prose-first summaries, evidence and risk where your eyes land, and anything that doesn't serve human review dropped from the page entirely rather than merely collapsed.

It stays queued behind the current work: M12 is still in flight, and its report — with the first real `ask` answers from your repo — is the next thing coming your way.
M12's dogfood answers are in — and they're the real thing. Verifying and committing (no other agents running, tree is all M12's):

attributes.command:
cd C:/src/git-for-ai && pnpm turbo build --force 2>&1 | grep "Tasks:" && cd packages/cli && pnpm vitest run 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests \|" ; cd ../.. && git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
M12: ask and blame --why - the CLI answers its founding question

Wires the M11 engine into the two commands the whole system exists
for, per ARCHITECTURE §9.1's exact output shapes, plus the review UI
ask panel going live (GET /api/ask; [n] citations link to change and
session pages; honest no-key/not-ready states; server stays GET-only
and non-minting, ref byte-identity asserted).

- queryDeps.ts: shared opener (config, query-side embedder,
  fingerprint checks); every not-ready state renders an actionable
  next step; stale index warns, never refuses.
- ask: synthesized cited answers with a deterministic Confidence line
  derived from retrieval signals (never model-claimed); no-key mode
  renders ranked sources with content - useful fully offline;
  --sources-only, --k, --since/--until (filtered between enrichment
  and synthesis so citations stay aligned), --json.
- blame --why <file>:<line>: works with no index at all (git-native
  reads); §9.1 template over the effective entry; synthesis opt-in
  via --explain; both degraded cases exit 2 with the git-metadata
  floor; Windows path/short-path handling fixed against a real
  failure.

56 new tests across cli/review-ui (all pin apiKey so the real key
cannot leak into tests); cli 144, review-ui 30, core 238, build and
typecheck green - independently re-verified.

Dogfooded on this repo with the real model and real key: ask
correctly explained the ref-relay elimination citing the actual
ledger entry and MONOREPO_PLAN sections; blame --why on resolve.ts:31
attributed the R4 redesign to its change with session pointer; the
pre-git-for-ai degraded case rendered exactly per CLI_REFERENCE.
CLI_PLAN §1 steps 4-5 now work for real.

Implemented by a background Fable 5 agent; reviewed and committed by
the orchestrating session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1
